description: PROVENANCE. Statically derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy, app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY, app/bms/COCRDUP.bms, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD and app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt, and NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL. Executing these programs is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS and no CICS emulator, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled and refuses a PROCEDURE ... USING program under -x, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters that break parsing outright, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from this repository altogether. That substitutes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else (AAP 0.7.6, practice B12, risk R-A, where the substitution is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than silently absorbed). Every byte below is read out of the source line ranges cited here and out of nothing else; the residual exposure is stated plainly, that a statically derived expectation can encode a misreading of the COBOL where a captured one could not, which is why every width below is taken mechanically from a PICTURE clause rather than from prose. THIS IS THE FOLDER'S TWENTIETH AND FINAL CASE, and it is the SOLE WITNESS FOR GATE G40 - the one EXEC CICS XCTL this program contains, projected as a nextProgram response field. THE UNIT IS THE CONTROLLER. unitKind is CONTROLLER_POJO: card.CardUpdateController is constructed through its own constructor over a fixture-backed card.CardRepository and a card.CardUpdateService built on that same repository, and updateCardDetail is called as a plain method on a plain object. There is NO MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no WebTestClient, no servlet container, no Spring application context and no JobLauncher anywhere in the path (gate G51). BATCH_JOB and COMPONENT are both illegal for this program and neither is used. THE PRECONDITION, :388-401. EIBCALEN is 489 and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is not LIT-MENUPGM, so BOTH disjuncts of the guard at :388-390 are false and the ELSE limb at :395-400 runs: MOVE DFHCOMMAREA (1:LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) restores the shared 160 bytes and MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1: LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) restores the program's own 329. That matters twice over: the inbound commarea SURVIVES rather than being discarded, which is the only reason the two fallback tests at :442-454 can see LOW-VALUES and the only reason the inbound CDEMO-USER-TYPE of 'A' is observable at all. Note the contrast with the sibling that arrives from the main menu, where INITIALIZE CARDDEMO-COMMAREA at :391 throws the inbound area away. THE STATE IS CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS, DELIBERATELY. CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION is 'S', the 88 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :281, which is the state 2000-DECIDE-ACTION arm (a) at :954-966 leaves behind once 9000-READ-DATA has found the card. It is deliberately NOT 'C' and NOT 'L' or 'F', and that choice is load-bearing: it makes arm one's second and third WHEN clauses FALSE, so the arm can only have been entered through its FIRST clause, on the attention identifier alone. A case that arrived in state 'C' could not tell the three clauses apart. THE AID SURVIVES COERCION, :413-424. SET PFK-INVALID TO TRUE runs unconditionally at :413. The validity test at :414-418 then admits exactly four combinations - CCARD-AID-ENTER OR CCARD-AID-PFK03 OR (CCARD-AID-PFK05 AND CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED) OR (CCARD-AID-PFK12 AND NOT CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED) - and PF3 matches the SECOND limb, which carries NO state qualification whatever. So PF3 exits from any state, PFK-VALID holds at :419, and the coercion IF PFK-INVALID SET CCARD-AID-ENTER TO TRUE at :422-424 DOES NOT FIRE. CCARD-AID is therefore 'PFK03' at exactly five bytes when the EVALUATE is reached. PF-KEY RESOLUTION, :406-407 AND app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy. PERFORM YYYY-STORE-PFKEY THRU YYYY-STORE-PFKEY-EXIT at :406-407 executes the body brought in by COPY 'CSSTRPFY' at :1528 - a copy statement that carries NO terminating period, the period sitting alone on :1529, and both quirks are left exactly as written (practice B5). THE COPYBOOK WAS READ AND ITS ARMS WERE COUNTED: it is a single ordered EVALUATE TRUE over EIBAID with TWENTY-EIGHT WHEN clauses and NO WHEN OTHER. DFHENTER maps to CCARD-AID-ENTER, DFHCLEAR to CLEAR, DFHPA1 and DFHPA2 to PA1 and PA2, DFHPF1 through DFHPF12 to PFK01 through PFK12, and then DFHPF13 through DFHPF24 FOLD BACK ONTO PFK01 THROUGH PFK12 - DFHPF13 to PFK01 at :54-55, DFHPF14 to PFK02, DFHPF15 to PFK03 at :58-59, and so on to DFHPF24 to PFK12 at :76-77. THAT CORRECTS THE SHORTER LIST THE PLANNING DOCUMENTS CARRY - DFHENTER, DFHCLEAR, DFHPA1, DFHPA2 and DFHPF1 through DFHPF12 - which covers only the first sixteen arms; the verified copybook has twenty-eight and the upper-bank fold is real behaviour, so the source wins and the divergence is documented rather than repaired (practice B4). TWO CONSEQUENCES ARE ASSERTED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLIED. FIRST, PF15 RESOLVES TO PFK03 AND THEREFORE REACHES THIS VERY EXIT: an EIBAID of DFHPF15 produces CCARD-AID 'PFK03' at :59, satisfies the second limb of :415 exactly as DFHPF3 does, and yields this case's expectation BYTE FOR BYTE - so a translation that implemented only the lower bank would answer the upper bank with a repainted screen instead of a hand-off. That correspondence is machine-checked by common.PfKeyResolver, whose DFHPF3 arm and DFHPF15 arm both return AidKey.PFK03, and by this program's COCRDUPCParityTest gate over all twenty-eight arms; this case declares DFHPF3 because it is the plain PF3 exit that gate G40 is about, and names the fold so a reviewer knows the same expectation covers DFHPF15. SECOND, AN UNRECOGNISED IDENTIFIER SILENTLY BECOMES ENTER: because CSSTRPFY has no WHEN OTHER, an EIBAID matching none of the twenty-eight leaves CCARD-AID at whatever it held, which is the LOW-VALUES that INITIALIZE CC-WORK-AREA at :374 put there, and that in turn fails the validity test and trips the coercion at :422-424 - so the request is processed as ENTER rather than rejected. The two mechanisms are SEPARATE and must not be collapsed: CSSTRPFY maps, and :413-424 coerces. Neither a raw AID byte nor a raw attribute byte is asserted anywhere in this case: DFHAID and DFHBMSCA are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D), so their values live in common.CicsAid and common.BmsAttributes, reproduced from IBM CICS documentation, and a case names a mnemonic. CCARD-AID'S SIXTEEN CONDITION NAMES, app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy:3-19. CCARD-AID is PIC X(5) and carries SIXTEEN 88-levels, not fifteen: ENTER, CLEAR, PA1 with VALUE 'PA1' space-padded to five, PA2 likewise, and PFK01 through PFK12. That count was taken by reading the copybook and it corrects the planning documents' fifteen (practice B4). CCARD-AID is asserted as 'PFK03' at exactly five bytes. ARM ONE OF THE MAIN EVALUATE, :429-476 (gate G30). The EVALUATE TRUE at :429 is first-match-wins and this case matches its VERY FIRST clause. ARM ONE HAS THREE WHEN CLAUSES SHARING ONE BODY, and all three are recorded because their order and their overlap are behaviour: :435 WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03; :436-437 WHEN (CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE AND CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET EQUAL LIT-CCLISTMAPSET); and :438-439 WHEN (CCUP-CHANGES-FAILED AND CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET EQUAL LIT-CCLISTMAPSET). The second becomes reachable after the 'C' outcome that the confirmed-save path produces, and the third after the 'L' and 'F' outcomes that the lock-failure and rewrite-failure paths produce, since 88 CCUP-CHANGES-FAILED at :288 covers both. Arm one also OUTRANKS arm four at :517-518, whose WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE and WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-FAILED repaint instead of navigating - so a commarea satisfying both must take arm one, and reversing the two would leave the operator on a screen the COBOL navigates away from. THE BODY, STATEMENT BY STATEMENT, :440-476. (1) SET CCARD-AID-PFK03 TO TRUE at :440 is REDUNDANT when PF3 was genuinely pressed, and it is preserved exactly because it is what makes the other two clauses converge on the same navigation and report PF3 to whatever reads the work area next (practice B5). (2) THE TRANSACTION FALLBACK, :442-447: IF CDEMO-FROM-TRANID EQUAL LOW-VALUES OR EQUAL SPACES then MOVE LIT-MENUTRANID TO CDEMO-TO-TRANID, ELSE MOVE CDEMO-FROM-TRANID TO CDEMO-TO-TRANID. LIT-MENUTRANID is PIC X(4) VALUE 'CM00' at :237-238. This case supplies LOW-VALUES and therefore takes the FALLBACK, so CDEMO-TO-TRANID is 'CM00'. (3) THE PROGRAM FALLBACK, :449-454: IF CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM EQUAL LOW-VALUES OR EQUAL SPACES then MOVE LIT-MENUPGM TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, ELSE MOVE CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM. LIT-MENUPGM is PIC X(8) VALUE 'COMEN01C' at :235-236. This case supplies LOW-VALUES and takes the FALLBACK, so CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is 'COMEN01C'. THE TWO ARE INDEPENDENT IF STATEMENTS OVER DIFFERENT FIELDS AND ARE ASSERTED AS TWO SEPARATE TESTS: a caller may supply one and not the other, in which case the target transaction and the target program come from different sources, and a translation that coupled them - one test governing both moves - would drift on exactly that input while passing this case. Both are tested as EQUAL LOW-VALUES OR EQUAL SPACES, two disjuncts reaching one MOVE, and LOW-VALUES IS THE STRICTLY STRONGER INPUT OF THE TWO, which is why it is the one declared: binary x'00' and a space are different bytes, so a translation that tested blankness alone would take the ELSE limb on a NUL-filled field and hand back a NUL-filled target, and only the low-values disjunct catches that. The same idiom appears again at :1013-1014 on CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, so an unset caller identity is a state this program genuinely anticipates in more than one place. (4) THE PROGRAM STAMPS ITSELF AS THE ORIGIN, :456-457: MOVE LIT-THISTRANID TO CDEMO-FROM-TRANID gives 'CCUP' at its PIC X(4) width, from :221-222, and MOVE LIT-THISPGM TO CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM gives 'COCRDUPC' at its PIC X(8) width, from :219-220, so the screen being navigated to can navigate back. THE ORDER OF (2), (3) AND (4) IS LOAD-BEARING AND THIS CASE IS THE SHAPE THAT PROVES IT: the two fallback tests read CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM BEFORE :456-457 overwrite them, so a translation that stamped itself first would find 'CCUP' and 'COCRDUPC' in those fields, take both ELSE limbs, and TRANSFER CONTROL TO ITSELF instead of to the menu. (5) THE CARRIED KEYS ARE ZEROED, :459-462: IF CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET EQUAL LIT-CCLISTMAPSET then MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM, where LIT-CCLISTMAPSET is PIC X(7) VALUE 'COCRDLI' at :231-232. THIS CASE SETS THE BRANCH UP TO FIRE, and the reason is coverage that no other shape in this folder provides: the inbound CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is 'COCRDLI', so both keys are zeroed and the assertion is that CDEMO-ACCT-ID becomes eleven zeros and CDEMO-CARD-NUM sixteen zeros even though real values - account 00000000050 and card 0500024453765740 - went in. The complementary branch, where the last mapset was this program's own and the two keys survive, is pinned by the sibling PF3 case that takes the ELSE limbs of :449-453. THE GUARD IS ALSO AN ORDERING ASSERTION: :459 reads CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET BEFORE :466 overwrites it with this program's own mapset, so a translation that stamped the mapset first would NEVER zero the keys on any input. AND THE ZEROING IS NARROW: only CDEMO-ACCT-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM are named, so CDEMO-CUST-ID stays at its inbound nine zeros and CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS stays at its inbound space - a translation that cleared the whole account or customer group would differ here. Note in passing that :1015-1017, on a different path, DOES additionally move LOW-VALUES to CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS, so the two clearings in this program are not the same clearing. (6) THE PRESERVED ODDITY, :464. SET CDEMO-USRTYP-USER TO TRUE is UNCONDITIONAL. It hard-codes CDEMO-USER-TYPE to 'U', the 88 at app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:28, REGARDLESS OF THE SIGNED-ON USER'S REAL TYPE, so an administrator who exits this screen is handed back to the menu as a plain user and loses the administrator flag. That is real behaviour, it is preserved rather than corrected (practice B5) and documented rather than quietly regularised (practice B4), and it is neither weakened nor unrequestedly strengthened - this program performs no authorisation of any kind and adding one would change the security posture the migration holds constant (practice B6). TO MAKE IT VISIBLE RATHER THAN MERELY DESCRIBED, THE INBOUND CDEMO-USER-TYPE IS 'A' AND THE OUTBOUND VALUE IS ASSERTED AS 'U'. That single pair is the sharpest assertion in this folder: an expectation that echoed the inbound 'A' would look far more reasonable and would be wrong. Note also what :464 does NOT touch: CDEMO-USER-ID is still 'ADMIN001' on the way out, so the identity is carried while only the type is overwritten, which is exactly the inconsistency worth pinning. (7) SET CDEMO-PGM-ENTER TO TRUE at :465 makes CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT the digit 0, the 88 at COCOM01Y:30. The inbound value is 1, CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at COCOM01Y:31, so the change is observable rather than a no-op. (8) MOVE LIT-THISMAPSET TO CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET at :466. LIT-THISMAPSET is PIC X(8) VALUE 'COCRDUP ' at :223-224 - EIGHT bytes, WITH A TRAILING SPACE - and CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is PIC X(7) at COCOM01Y:44. A COBOL alphanumeric MOVE truncates on the RIGHT, so the trailing space is dropped and the receiver holds 'COCRDUP' at exactly SEVEN bytes. That is derived from the two declared widths, not assumed, and it is asserted at seven. (9) MOVE LIT-THISMAP TO CDEMO-LAST-MAP at :467 gives 'CCRDUPA' from LIT-THISMAP PIC X(7) at :225-226, which is the map name the CCRDUPA DFHMDI label declares at app/bms/COCRDUP.bms:25 under the COCRDUP DFHMSD at :20 - so the stored map name and the physical map agree. (10) EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT at :469-471. It has no counterpart in the expectation and needs none: this arm performs no file I/O at all, and the one paragraph that writes opens and commits its own unit of work, so there is nothing outstanding for a syncpoint to commit. GATE G40 - THE XCTL BECOMES A RESPONSE FIELD. EXEC CICS XCTL is on :473, its PROGRAM (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) operand on :474, COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) on :475, and END-EXEC on :476. Both citations in circulation refer to this ONE site - the plan's L474 names the PROGRAM operand line and the card package's L473 names the statement line - so it is cited here as the XCTL at :473-476 whose PROGRAM operand is on :474, and the discrepancy is reconciled rather than left to look like two sites (practice B4). IT IS THE ONLY XCTL IN THIS PROGRAM: an exhaustive search finds exactly one, the other textual hit being the comment at :433. It is one of the migration's eight XCTL sites and one of the four COMMAREA-driven XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) shapes, the others being in COACTUPC, COACTVWC and COCRDSLC. THE JAVA FORM IS A nextProgram RESPONSE FIELD ECHOED FROM common.NavigationContext AND RESOLVED CLIENT-SIDE: nextProgram is asserted as 'COMEN01C', identical to the CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM the navigation carries, and there is NO server-side forward, NO redirect chain and NO session affinity. termination is XCTL and not RETURN_TRANSID, and the two are not interchangeable. ARM ONE NEVER REACHES COMMON-RETURN, AND ITS ABSENCES ARE POSITIVE ASSERTIONS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS. Control transfers at :473, so the MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO CCARD-ERROR-MSG at :547, the assembly of WS-COMMAREA PIC X(2000) at :549-552 and the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID (LIT-THISTRANID) COMMAREA (WS-COMMAREA) at :554-558 DO NOT EXECUTE. So: no RETURN TRANSID occurs; nothing is moved into CCARD-ERROR-MSG; and arm one performs NO 3000-SEND-MAP, which is why sends is EMPTY and why THIS CASE CARRIES NO SEVENTEEN-FIELD SCREEN EXPECTATION AT ALL. That absence is stated so it cannot be read as a gap: the seventeen xxxO payload items of app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY - TRNNAME 4, TITLE01 40, CURDATE 8, PGMNAME 8, TITLE02 40, CURTIME 8, ACCTSID 11, CARDSID 16, CRDNAME 50, CRDSTCD 1, EXPMON 2, EXPYEAR 4, EXPDAY 2, INFOMSG 40, ERRMSG 80, FKEYS 21, FKEYSC 18 - are pinned by the cases that reach 3000-SEND-MAP, and pinning them here would claim a send this arm does not perform. For the same reason nextMapset, nextMap and cursorField are DELIBERATELY ABSENT: CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP, both PIC X(7) in app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy:23-24, are never assigned on this arm and stay at their initialised spaces, which is not a BMS map name, and no MOVE -1 into an xxxL length item happens because no map is sent - so the faithful report is that no map, mapset or cursor was named. GATE G37 AND RULE R6 - THE WHOLE CONVERSATION IS PAYLOAD. No server-side state exists anywhere in this case: no HttpSession, no server-side cache, no static mutable field, and no session affinity - the response is a pure function of the request. EIBCALEN is 160 + 329 = 489. The 160 is the shared CARDDEMO-COMMAREA of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, whose sixteen items are summed here by hand rather than quoted (practice B11): CDEMO-FROM-TRANID 4 plus CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM 8 plus CDEMO-TO-TRANID 4 plus CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM 8 plus CDEMO-USER-ID 8 plus CDEMO-USER-TYPE 1 plus CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 plus CDEMO-CUST-ID 9 plus CDEMO-CUST-FNAME 25 plus CDEMO-CUST-MNAME 25 plus CDEMO-CUST-LNAME 25 plus CDEMO-ACCT-ID 11 plus CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS 1 plus CDEMO-CARD-NUM 16 plus CDEMO-LAST-MAP 7 plus CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET 7, which is 34 plus 84 plus 12 plus 16 plus 14, equalling 160 exactly. The 329 is WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :274-321: CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION 1 plus CCUP-OLD-DETAILS 89, being 11 plus 16 plus 3 plus 50 plus 4 plus 2 plus 2 plus 1, plus CCUP-NEW-DETAILS 89 with the identical shape, plus CARD-UPDATE-RECORD 150, being 16 plus 11 plus 3 plus 50 plus 10 plus 1 plus the FILLER X(59) at :321 - and 1 plus 89 plus 89 plus 150 is 329. Those two sums are the self-check: a field dropped or a FILLER shortened makes a total wrong immediately. A GENUINE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THIS EXIT AND EVERY OTHER PATH, DERIVED FROM :475 RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the XCTL passes CARDDEMO-COMMAREA AND NOTHING ELSE, so on this path the 160 bytes TRAVEL and the 329 DO NOT. The program being transferred to receives 160; handing it 489 would give it state the source never passes. On every other path COMMON-RETURN assembles both halves into WS-COMMAREA - bytes 1 to 160 at :549 and 161 to 489 at :550-552 - and that assembly is exactly what this case asserts did not happen. The inbound 329-byte trailer is nevertheless declared in full, because the case must state its own complete pre-state rather than imply it (practice B9), and because the state character it carries is what makes arm one's clause selection unambiguous. GATE G34 - ALL THREE CVCRD01Y REDEFINITIONS, ROUND-TRIPPED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy declares THREE REDEFINES pairs, not one, and each is two typed accessors over ONE backing span: CC-ACCT-ID PIC X(11) VALUE SPACES with CC-ACCT-ID-N REDEFINES CC-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) at :34-36; CC-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) VALUE SPACES with CC-CARD-NUM-N REDEFINES CC-CARD-NUM PIC 9(16) at :37-39; and CC-CUST-ID PIC X(09) VALUE SPACES with CC-CUST-ID-N REDEFINES CC-CUST-ID PIC 9(9) at :40-42. Each round-trips both ways: writing 50 through CC-ACCT-ID-N and reading CC-ACCT-ID back yields '00000000050', the zero-padded digit string at the FULL eleven-byte width rather than a trimmed '50', and writing '00000000050' through the alphanumeric view and reading CC-ACCT-ID-N back yields 50; writing 500024453765740 through CC-CARD-NUM-N yields '0500024453765740' at sixteen, and the reverse yields 500024453765740; and writing 1 through CC-CUST-ID-N yields '000000001' at nine, with the reverse yielding 1. THE THIRD PAIR IS THE REASON IT IS LISTED HERE: CC-CUST-ID and CC-CUST-ID-N are NOT OTHERWISE EXERCISED BY COCRDUPC ANYWHERE - the program moves the account id at :490 and :1463 and the card number at :491 and :1425, and never touches the customer id - so this final case is the folder's ONLY place that pair is round-tripped, and leaving it out would leave one of the three redefinitions unproven. THE COMMENTED-OUT ITEMS STAY UNMODELLED. CVCRD01Y also carries CCARD-LAST-PROG at :20, CCARD-RETURN-TO-PROG at :22, CCARD-RETURN-FLAG with its two 88-levels at :25-27, and CCARD-FUNCTION with its two 88-levels at :31-33, ALL COMMENTED OUT. They are not resurrected (practice B5). The ACTIVE members are exactly CCARD-AID X(5), CCARD-NEXT-PROG X(8), CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET X(7), CCARD-NEXT-MAP X(7), CCARD-ERROR-MSG X(75) and CCARD-RETURN-MSG X(75), plus the three identifier spans above. NEGATIVE ASSERTIONS, EACH VERIFIED BY EXHAUSTIVE SEARCH RATHER THAN ASSUMED. NO CARDAIX ACCESS AT ALL (gate G45, in its strongest form). LIT-CARDFILENAME-ACCT-PATH PIC X(8) VALUE 'CARDAIX ' is declared at :253-254 and REFERENCED NOWHERE ELSE IN THE PROGRAM, and both MOVE CC-ACCT-ID-N TO WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID statements that would have populated the alternate key, at :1379 and :1424, are COMMENTED OUT and stay that way (practice B5). So COCRDUPC never reads the alternate-index path, and this case asserts zero CARDAIX access. The alternate index exists only as a FINDER METHOD ON THE SINGLE CardRepository - never a second repository and never a second table - which app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD makes plain by defining CARDAIX at :13-14 as a DSNAME ending VSAM.AIX.PATH over the very base cluster CARDDAT names at :25-26; the test profile accordingly binds CARDDAT, CARDFILE and CARDAIX to one dataset. The planning documents list this program against two datasets, CARDAIX and CARDDAT; the verified source uses one, and the divergence is documented rather than silently adopted (practice B4). NO SCHEMA ARTEFACT OF ANY KIND (gate G44): no DDL, no schema migration, no entity annotation, no version column, no timestamp column, no sequence column and no generated table definition appears in this case or in the code it drives - the program's concurrency control is the field-by-field re-read comparison of 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC, and replacing it with a version column would be precisely the schema change the migration forbids. NO THANK-YOU AND NO INVALID-KEY TEXT. COCRDUPC references only CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 from its title and message copybooks, at :1057-1058; app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy's CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU and CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY have ZERO references in the program. Their absence is asserted, and the two thank-you literals are kept apart rather than conflated: CSMSG01Y:18-19 declares CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU PIC X(50) VALUE 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...' padded to fifty, while app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:23-24 declares a DIFFERENT string, CCDA-THANK-YOU PIC X(40) VALUE 'Thank you for using CCDA application...' padded to forty. Neither appears in any expectation here. NO USER AND NO CUSTOMER RECORD ACCESS. COPY CSUSR01Y at :346 and COPY CVCUS01Y at :359 are both present, yet a search for SEC-USR and for CUST- returns ZERO field references in the program: the copybooks are declared and unused, and declared-but-unused stays unmodelled (practice B5). This case reads no user record and no customer record. Two further copies, CVACT01Y at :350 and CVACT03Y at :356, are themselves commented out. CSSETATY IS NOT COPIED BY THIS PROGRAM. Its full copy list is CVCRD01Y at :268, COCOM01Y at :272, DFHBMSCA at :327, DFHAID at :328, COTTL01Y at :332, COCRDUP at :334, CSDAT01Y at :337, CSMSG01Y at :340, CSMSG02Y at :343, CSUSR01Y at :346, CVACT02Y at :353, CVCUS01Y at :359 and CSSTRPFY at :1528 - THIRTEEN copies and NO CSSETATY. The DFHRED plus asterisk highlighting is written INLINE at :1243-1307, and its guards differ by field group: the two search keys are highlighted under the REENTER context test at :1248 while the four data fields are highlighted under CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK from :1264 onward. That correction is recorded (practice B4), and none of it is exercised on this path because arm one performs no 3000-SEND-MAP. NO WRITE, NO ADD, NO DELETE AND NO BROWSE. Arm one performs NO FILE ACCESS WHATSOEVER, so expectedWrites is EMPTY as a POSITIVE assertion that nothing was written rather than as an absence of interest, and expectedFinalState and expectedDatasets are empty because the unit under test is the controller on a path that opens nothing - there is no dataset channel to report and asserting one would claim an access that never happened. NO ABEND. There is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in COCRDUPC - zero occurrences - so expectedReturnCode is 0 and gate G35 is INAPPLICABLE rather than merely unasserted. NO MESSAGE IS EMITTED. SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF TO TRUE at :384 clears the message before the dispatch, nothing on this arm writes to WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) at :173, and the MOVE at :547 that would have carried it to the screen is never reached because control transfers at :473 - so expectedMessages is empty, and that is an honest statement of what the unit emits rather than an invented screen. NO NORMALISATION IS DECLARED, and that too is a measurement: carddata.txt rows are already the full 150 bytes with a space-filled FILLER, and the two markers the contract defines belong to cardxref, whose rows are 36 bytes against a 50-byte copybook, and to USRSEC. THE SEED, AND WHY IT IS INERT HERE. CARDDAT is seeded from rows 0 to 2 of src/test/resources/fixtures/carddata.txt, which is byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt, at the 150-byte CVACT02Y width - row 0 being card 0500024453765740 on account 00000000050, CVV 747, embossed name 'Aniya Von' padded to fifty, expiring 2023-03-09, status Y, with FILLER X(59) closing the record, and 16 plus 11 plus 3 plus 50 plus 10 plus 1 plus 59 summing to 150.
